title: Conservative rollforward autoscaler and burst harmonizer
author: Aisha Gupta
description:
Motivation: Production fleets sometimes oscillate when autoscalers attempt aggressive roll-forward reallocation after transient load spikes. This PR introduces a conservative 'roll-forward' autoscaler mode plus a burst harmonizer that smooths burst credit consumption across tenants to avoid thrashing, reduce tail latency regressions, and keep utilization telemetry meaningful for decision-making.

What this changes: single continuous description of changes and rationale. The new autoscaler mode adds a multi-window evaluation that prefers smaller capacity increments and requires cross-window agreement before committing large increases (default parameters conservative_rollforward_window=5m, consensus_factor=0.6). The burst harmonizer is a lightweight controller that smooths short-term burst drains into a soft reservoir, exposing metrics that let the fleet admission layer de-prioritize noncritical bursts when headroom is low.

Key features:
- Conservative rollforward policy: incremental scaling steps, weighted by recent utilization quantiles (p50/p95/p99) and a stability score to avoid oscillation.
- Burst harmonizer: credits smoothing, decay curve tuning, and tenant bucketing to balance fairness during cluster-wide surges.
- New telemetry: fleet_rollforward_score, harmonizer_slack, tenant_burst_lead and burst_decay_delta (see docs/design/autoscaler-rollforward.md).
- Canary-safe rollout: feature gated behind config: autoscaler.mode=conservative; default remains the existing autoscaler. Includes a canary flag and rollout plan in cmd/fleetctl/config.yaml.
- Backwards compatibility: config knobs map to existing autoscaler hooks; no schema changes to persisted reservation ledgers.

Operational knobs (examples):
- conservative_rollforward_step: "+10%" (max per-commit growth)
- conservative_rollforward_window: "300s"
- harmonizer_decay_half_life: "60s"

Testing and verification: unit tests for the stabilization logic + integration test simulating a 10x spike across 250 tenants. Local performance tests show reduced oscillation (measured as reallocate cycles per minute) by ~72% in the synthetic scenario.

Related: ENG-1987 implements the rollout plan; ENG-2021 requested tenant-level fairness constraints. SUP-4123 is an on-call incident that motivated the harmonizer because burst drains caused a partial SLA regression during a cross-tenant traffic event.

Checklist:

- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration test added
- [x] Metrics and dashboards updated

Merge notes: squash merge. The feature defaults to opt-in and the rollout will be controlled via fleet config and canary labels.
